summary.headline: Home First Q1 FY27: AUM up 25.7% YoY to INR16,938 crore and PAT up 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, with stable asset quality.
summary.overview: Home First delivered strong Q1 FY27 growth, with AUM at INR16,938 crore (up 25.7% YoY, 6.7% QoQ) and disbursements of INR1,628 crore (up 31.0% YoY). Profit after tax rose 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, driven by 38.2% growth in net interest income and NIM expanding to 6.0% from 5.9%. Asset quality was flat across 1+ DPD (4.7%), 30+ DPD (3.2%) and GS3 (1.8%), and management said Q1 collections were better than usual. CFO Nutan Patwari will step down from executive responsibilities effective August 31, 2026, and the Board is evaluating candidates for the role.

financial_highlights.change: ROA +10 bps QoQ, ROE +50 bps QoQ

segments.name: Home loans (individual housing)
segments.commentary: 83% of portfolio; management said growth in both origination and disbursements was led by home loans, with housing ticket sizes up marginally.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 13-14% of portfolio; LAP growth was lower than home loans and ticket sizes were unchanged. NPA levels are broadly in line with home loans.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Co-lending book INR617 crore (3.6% of AUM); Q1 disbursements INR46 crore. Management cited process and policy changes causing hiccups that are being addressed.

guidance_outlook: Spread ex co-lending to stay within 5% to 5.25% long-term range; book spread 5.30% and incremental spread 5.40% in Q1.
Opex to AUM guided at 2.6% to 2.7% for full year; reported Q1 figure was 2.8%.
Credit cost of 40 bps in Q1; BT out expected to hold in roughly the 5% ballpark, not yet committed to 4.5% sustaining.
PLR cut considered unlikely at present given West Asia uncertainty.
NHB drawdown (currently nil, outstanding INR354 crore) planned for Q2 FY27.
Repayment rate assumption of 16% to 17% used in planning.
capex_capacity: Added four branches in Q1 (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh), taking network to 175 branches and 373 touch points.
Net addition of 133 employees in Q1, taking headcount to 1,988; management said employees per branch rose by about one person.
Green Homes: 100 homes certified in Q1, cumulative 550 certified as of June 2026.
Cue (in-house AI omnichannel communications platform) operationalised; bureau analyzer and bank statement analysis model in production; AI pilots in lead qualification, valuation and income analysis.
demand_pricing: Disbursement growth of 31% YoY split roughly 50:50 between volume (units) and ticket size, per management.

Origination yield 13.0%; portfolio yield ex co-lending 13.1%. Management said yields are held by serving the same customer segment; marginal long-term yield compression expected and to be offset by opex.
Incremental cost of borrowing 7.6%; cost of borrowing 7.8% (down 10 bps QoQ). Loan book is fully floating except one NHB scheme fixed for 7 years.
INR25 lakh-plus ticket share rose to 18% from about 12% two to three years ago; management says spreads are not materially different across ticket sizes.
BT out fell to 4.5% in Q1, the lowest in several quarters; management attributed this to internal protocols (branch-level top-up pitches) rather than industry change.
Login-to-sanction ratio about 40%; origination volume growth about 10-15%.
Repayment rate 14.3% in Q1 per analyst calculation vs about 16% last year; management said there is no change in prepayment behaviour.
Stress from Surat and Tirupur tariff-affected pockets has eased; Tamil Nadu recovering after tariff and team issues.
Long-term growth focus: Uttar Pradesh, plus Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in the next 1-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7.6% incremental cost of borrowing sustainable, and is there a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no one-off; the NHB drawdown has not been taken (INR354 crore outstanding at both March and June), with a drawdown planned for Q2. Spreads are guided to a 5% to 5.25% range; book spread is 5.30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BT out fall to 4.5%, and is this industry-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited internal branch-level processes started about 5-6 quarters ago. It expects BT out in roughly the 5% range and would not commit to 4.5% without 2-3 quarters of confirmation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year opex-to-AUM guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year guidance is 2.6% to 2.7%, with a YoY reduction of 5 to 10 bps expected. Q1 opex rose due to increments and fresh hiring.

qa_highlights.question: Why was co-lending momentum weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw hiccups from changes in co-lending process and policy; management said partner banks are aligning and numbers should stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the source of disbursement growth: volume or ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 50% of growth came from unit volume and 50% from ticket size. Origination volume grew about 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for delinquencies after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 collections were excellent, with stable or improved buckets, and expects stable numbers across quarters, though Q1 is usually a seasonal uptick period.

risks_watch: Spread durability: book spread 5.30% vs incremental 5.40% and 7.6% incremental cost of borrowing; management says no one-off, but the NHB drawdown (INR354 crore, nil taken in Q1) is planned for Q2 FY27, so the Q2 borrowing cost mix is a key check.

BT out: fell to 4.5% in Q1, first quarter below 5%; management would not commit to 4.5% sustaining and needs 2-3 quarters of confirmation before guiding lower. Watch whether it returns to the 5-6% range.
Opex to AUM: Q1 reported at 2.8% vs full-year guidance of 2.6-2.7%; the company needs a 5-10 bps YoY reduction, with hiring and increments adding cost.
Co-lending: disbursements of INR46 crore in Q1 and a weak run attributed to process and policy changes at partner banks; track whether partner alignment restores volumes.
Collections and delinquencies: 1+ DPD 4.7%, 30+ DPD 3.2%, GS3 1.8%; Q1 collections were called excellent, but management expects a seasonal uptick in Q1 and wants stable numbers across quarters.
CFO transition: Nutan Patwari steps down from executive responsibilities effective August 31, 2026; the Board has not yet named a successor.
key_quotes: We remain confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while maintaining our focus on profitability, portfolio quality and operating efficiency.
But whether it will sustain at 4.5% is difficult to say. Of course, it has been an extraordinarily good quarter in that sense.
This time, the first quarter has been excellent in terms of collections. So hopefully, that trend should continue, and we should be able to keep these numbers stable across quarters.
Except for a particular scheme of NHB where the loan is fixed for 7 years, the rest of the portfolio is all floating.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth, asset quality and collections, and it committed to the 25% AUM growth target and the 5% to 5.25% spread range. It was cautious on BT out sustainability and would not commit to the 4.5% level. It gave evasive answers on the PLR and the CFO successor, saying only that the Board is evaluating candidates.

adds.what: Four new branches added in Q1 (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh), taking network to 175 branches and 373 touch points

growth.why: Management reiterated 25% AUM growth for FY27 (AUM up 25.7% YoY in Q1) backed by disbursements up 31% YoY, origination volume growth of 10-15%, and a branch network expansion of four branches in Q1, though no specific capacity or order numbers were given beyond that.

mgmt.note: CFO Nutan Patwari will step down from executive responsibilities effective August 31, 2026, and the Board is evaluating candidates; no stated growth plan from successor.
